newsitem.title: BRAZIL: U.S. Daley urges FTAA countries to address tariffs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Daley urges FTAA countries to address tariffs.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Secretary William Daley, who is visiting Brazil to discuss the creation of a free trade zone across the Americas, said on Monday that difficult issues like import tariffs had to be discussed sooner rather than later.

Trade ministers from 34 countries in the Americas, excluding Cuba, are meeting in the Brazilian industrial city of Belo Horizonte on May 14-16 to hammer out a deal on setting up the Free Trade Area of the Americas (FTAA), which leaders at the 1994 Miami summit agreed to set up by 2005.

"In order to reach the goal of 2005 we have to deal with the difficult issues like market access up front," Daley told reporters at an American Chamber of Commerce lunch in Rio de Janeiro, the first stop on his 11-day tour of South America.
Brazil and its partners in the Mercosur customs union have been advocating a more gradual approach, hoping to leave any talks on the lowering of import tariffs until 2003.

Brazil fears the effects of a rapid market opening to competitive U.S. products following the shock of liberalisaing trade over the past three years. It believes its efforts have not been met by a similar U.S. readiness to reduce non-tariff barriers blocking Brazilian orange juice and steel exports.

Daley said he hoped ministers at Belo Horizonte would agree that FTAA negotiations should proceed according to a specific schedule after a presidential summit of the 34 nations in Santiago, Chile, next March.

"We hope to come out of Belo (Horizonte) with a specific game plan so that come Santiago we have specific deadlines," Daley said. "The negotiations must begin after March in a very aggressive and specific way."

He said he was hopeful the U.S. government would get "fast track" authority from Congress "well before" the Santiago summit to conduct the FTAA negotiations. He said fast track authority was not necessary for talks, but was seen by other nations as a "litmus test of our commitment to open markets".

Daley said the U.S. was "eager" to address Brazil's trade worries, but added that the U.S. government viewed with concern Brazil's 1995 car industry regime which was a "clear violation" of World Trade Organisation (WTO) rules.
He said the United States would consider taking Brazil to the WTO over the regime, but hoped the matter could be resolved through talks.
